ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A pair of wedges are located on a horizontal surface. The coefficient of friction (both sliding and static) between the wedges is $\mu$, the coefficient of friction between the bottom wedge B and the horizontal surface is also $\mu$. The angle of the wedge is $\theta$. The mass of the top wedge A is $m$, and the mass of the bottom wedge B is $M = 2m$. A horizontal force $F$ directed to the left is applied to the bottom wedge as shown in the figure. Assume $g = 9.8 \, \text{N/kg}$.

1. Determine the range of values for $F$ so that the top wedge does not slip on the bottom wedge. Express your answer(s) in terms of any or all of $m$, $g$, $\theta$, and $\mu$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure, the lower wedge B is placed on the horizontal ground, and its upper surface is an inclined plane slanting from lower left to upper right, with the angle between the inclined plane and the horizontal plane labeled θ. The upper wedge A is placed on the inclined plane of B. The right side of wedge B is subjected to a horizontal leftward external force F, and the arrow in the figure points left. The figure also labels the two wedges A and B. Reasoning: According to the problem requirement, A does not slide relative to B, therefore A and B have a common horizontal leftward acceleration a. Take the upward direction along the inclined plane as the positive tangential direction, with the unit tangential direction along the upper right; take the direction perpendicular to the inclined plane outward as the normal direction. For the forces on A: gravity mg, the supporting force N of the inclined plane on A, and static friction force f along the inclined plane. The acceleration of A is horizontal leftward, with magnitude a. Write Newton's second law along the inclined plane direction: f - mg sinθ = m(-a cosθ), so f = m(g sinθ - a cosθ). Write Newton's second law along the normal direction: N - mg cosθ = m(a sinθ), so N = m(g cosθ + a sinθ). The no-sliding condition is |f| ≤ μN, therefore |g sinθ - a cosθ| ≤ μ(g cosθ + a sinθ). Divide both sides by cosθ, let tanθ = t, and obtain |g t - a| ≤ μ(g + a t). From this, obtain the allowed range of the common acceleration: a ≥ g(t - μ)/(1 + μt), and a ≤ g(t + μ)/(1 - μt), that is, a ∈ [g(tanθ - μ)/(1 + μ tanθ), g(tanθ + μ)/(1 - μ tanθ)]. Then regard A+B as a whole, with total mass 3m. The external force in the horizontal direction is leftward F, and the friction force from the ground on B is rightward. According to the given method, take its magnitude as μ(3mg). Therefore F - 3μmg = 3ma, that is, F = 3m(a + μg). Substitute the lower end of the acceleration: F_min = 3mg[μ + (tanθ - μ)/(1 + μ tanθ)] = 3mg[(1 + μ^2)tanθ/(1 + μ tanθ)]. Substitute the upper end of the acceleration: F_max = 3mg[μ + (tanθ + μ)/(1 - μ tanθ)] = 3mg[2μ + (1 - μ^2)tanθ]/(1 - μ tanθ).
